text:
Let the unit vector in the \(x\)-\(z\) plane be

\[
\vec n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta).
\]

The spin operator along \(\vec n\) is

\[
P_{\vec n}=\vec n\cdot \vec P
=\frac{\hbar}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & -\cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

For eigenvalue \(+\hbar/2\), write the eigenvector as \((a,b)^T\). The eigenvalue equation gives

\[
\frac{b}{a}=\frac{1-\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}
=\tan\frac{\theta}{2}.
\]

Thus, up to an arbitrary overall phase,

\[
a=\cos\frac{\theta}{2},\qquad b=\sin\frac{\theta}{2}.
\]

This vector is normalized because \(\cos^2(\theta/2)+\sin^2(\theta/2)=1\). The factor \(\hbar\) belongs to the eigenvalue, not to the eigenvector components.

Answer: B
